office_does: The District 5 councilmember is one of seven Pierce County Council members who adopt the county budget, ordinances, taxes and land-use rules for an area including Fife, the Port of Tacoma, Parkland and parts of Spanaway and Tacoma.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Bryan Yambe, appointed in 2025 after eleven years on the Fife City Council, faces Republican Bettina Gese, a Puyallup Tribal member and small-business owner; Yambe took 61.5% in the primary. The race turns on Yambe's votes for the county's public-safety sales tax and budget versus Gese's call to cut taxes and spending.

candidates.summary: Appointed councilmember since 2025 and former Fife deputy mayor, running on affordable housing, public safety with crisis response, food security and transportation investment.
highlights: Voted for the 0.1% criminal-justice sales tax (passed 5-2) and the 2026-2027 budget (passed 4-3) [S7][S8]
Says his first year helped secure $12.2 million creating or preserving 646 affordable homes [S3][S12]
Voted for the cottage-housing ordinance expanding housing options [S9]
Pairs first-responder funding with crisis response and youth intervention [S3][S4]
Endorsed by Gov. Bob Ferguson, the Central Labor Council and Washington Conservation Action [S5]

taxes.basis: Voted for the council-imposed 0.1% criminal-justice sales tax and campaigns on it as the 'Justice Fund'; a flat sales tax, and he also promotes senior and low-income property-tax relief.

spending.basis: Voted for the 2026-2027 budget and campaigns on expanded housing, childcare, behavioral-health, food and transit investment.

housing.basis: Leads with public affordable-housing funding, rapid rehousing and homebuyer programs, alongside permit streamlining and a yes vote on cottage housing.

safety.basis: Leads with law enforcement, fire and EMS investment and voted for the tax funding deputy hiring, while emphasizing crisis response, youth intervention and a 'fairer justice system'.

climate.basis: Platform calls for 'the urgent local action required to mitigate climate change'.

experience.basis: Sitting councilmember with eleven prior years on the Fife City Council and several regional board seats, running on what he has 'delivered'.

candidates.summary: Puyallup Tribal member, former geoduck diver, real-estate agent and small-business owner running on lower taxes, spending restraint, infrastructure and public safety.
highlights: Pledges to 'push back on unnecessary tax increases': 'we have a spending problem' [S3]
Would prioritize neglected roads and bridges, including the Canyon Road project and the War Memorial and Milroy bridges [S3][S7]
Would streamline permitting while protecting single-family neighborhoods from denser development [S3]
Frames public safety around accountability for repeat crime and recovery pathways to 'end the revolving door' [S3][S7]
Endorsed by the Puyallup Tribe of Indians [S2]

taxes.basis: Runs under a 'Lower Taxes' plank pledging to resist unnecessary tax increases and protect families from rising costs.

spending.basis: Says 'we don't have a money problem — we have a spending problem', would cut wasteful spending while protecting essential programs, and pledges transparent spending.

housing.basis: Would cut costs, streamline permitting and increase supply 'where it makes sense', while opposing denser development in single-family neighborhoods.

safety.basis: Emphasizes accountability for repeat crime and says 'enabling destructive behavior under the guise of compassion helps no one', while backing recovery pathways.

experience.basis: First-time candidate who presents herself as 'not a career politician' against a sitting incumbent.
